answer: A stake-weighted reputation system works like a river: every agent must lock a refundable bond before it can trade, so spinning up fake identities costs real capital. When one identity misbehaves, the penalty sends a ripple through its whole trust graph, lowering the standing of every account linked to it. An honest newcomer starts as a small ember — limited volume until repeated good behavior proves it — so a sybil flood can never outrun the cost of building trust.
